Income Tax Return is not just a compliance requirement in India, but it also acts as a financial identity document when applying for a visa. Most countries such as the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, and Schengen countries require ITR for:

Proof of income and financial stability
Evidence of lawful earnings

At IGSK & Associates, we specialize in Income Tax Return (ITR) filing for individuals, ensuring that you not only remain compliant with tax laws but also maximize your refund from TDS (Tax Deducted at Source).

If you are a salaried employee, freelancer, or investor, there is a high possibility that excess TDS has been deducted from your income. Filing your Income Tax Return correctly is the only way to claim your rightful refund from the Income Tax Department.

🔍 What is TDS and Why Refund Arises?

TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) is deducted by employers, banks, or other payers before making payments to you. However, in many cases:

Your total income falls below taxable limits
You are eligible for deductions under various sections
Excess TDS is deducted due to incorrect declarations
Bank interest or other incomes attract higher TDS

This results in extra tax being paid, which can be claimed back only through proper ITR filing.

✅ Who Should File ITR for TDS Refund?

You should definitely file your Income Tax Return if:

TDS is deducted from your salary or bank interest
You have Form 16 or Form 16A showing deductions
You have investments eligible for deductions
Your income is below taxable limits but TDS is deducted
You want to carry forward losses (stocks, mutual funds, etc.)
You want to avoid notices from the Income Tax Department

Even if your income is not taxable, filing ITR is essential
